reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) shows that melt-spinning at 33 m/s yields an amorphous structure, but provides no data on wheel speeds above 33 m/s, no measurements of free volume or atomic disorder, and no comparison of crystallization onset temperatures at different wheel speeds. The premises about increased free volume, delayed crystallization, and uniform cooling at 50 m/s are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Increasing melt-spinning wheel speed from ~30 to 50 m/s significantly increases the cooling rate
Higher cooling rate increases atomic disorder and retained free volume in the amorphous phase
Increased free volume and disorder suppress crystallization, raising the crystallization onset temperature
Uniform cooling across the ribbon is achievable with diagnostic controls at 50 m/s
The alloy system studied (CrMnFeCoNiP) is representative of phosphorus-containing HEAs
